whatIsPatent.label: UNDERSTANDING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
whatIsPatent.heading: What is a Patent?
whatIsPatent.quote: “A patent gives an inventor a legal right over an invention for a limited period, subject to the requirements of patent law.”
whatIsPatent.desc1: A patent is intended to protect an invention by giving the patent holder exclusive rights, in exchange for publicly disclosing the invention.
whatIsPatent.desc2: By publishing the technical specification, the inventor enriches global scientific knowledge while securing sovereign legal recourse against unauthorized replication.
whatIsPatent.whyDesc: Patents can help inventors protect new and useful inventions, discourage unauthorized use, and create a foundation for commercialisation.
whatIsPatent.whyNote: *Patentability is contingent upon satisfying statutory thresholds of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability under the Indian Patents Act.
whatIsPatent.protectDesc: Confers legal exclusivity to prevent third parties from unauthorized making, using, offering for sale, or importing the invention.
whatIsPatent.discloseDesc: Enriches public technical knowledge through mandatory publication, inspiring subsequent innovations while maintaining sovereign priority.
whatIsPatent.commercialiseDesc: Transforms scientific breakthroughs into valuable intellectual property assets for licensing, institutional partnerships, and commercial scale.
whatIsPatent.scrollSub: Discover how an Indian patent moves from idea to grant.

patentProcess.heading: The Indian Patent Process
patentProcess.subtitle: From preliminary novelty clearance to the sovereign Letters Patent grant under the Patents Act, 1970.

step1.title: Prior Art & Clearance
step1.subtitle: Novelty Assessment & TKDL Defensive Search
step1.description: Assess statutory patentability under Section 2(1)(j) and Section 3. Conduct exhaustive clearance searches across global patent databases, IPO INPASS, and the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) to verify novelty and inventive step prior to filing.
step1.keyAction: Verify Section 3 eligibility & search TKDL prior art

step2.title: Drafting Specification
step2.subtitle: Technical Claims & Biological Declarations
step2.description: Draft the Provisional or Complete Specification under Form 2. Formulate precise legal claims, detailed embodiments, and mandatory statutory disclosures declaring the geographical source of biological materials under Section 10(4)(d)(ii).
step2.keyAction: Formulate precise claims & declare biological origins

step3.title: Filing the Application
step3.subtitle: Jurisdictional Submission & Priority Date
step3.description: Submit Form 1 alongside Form 3 (Foreign Filing Undertaking) and Form 5 (Inventorship) across the appropriate IPO jurisdiction (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, or Kolkata) to secure sovereign priority date and official CBR receipt.
step3.keyAction: Submit Forms 1, 3 & 5 to secure priority date

step4.title: Official Gazette Publication
step4.subtitle: 18-Month Disclosure & Early Publication Option
step4.description: The application is published in the official Patent Journal under Section 11A after 18 months, or expedited within 1 month via Form 9. Publication invites public scrutiny and opens the statutory window for pre-grant opposition under Section 25(1).

step5.title: Substantive Review & FER
step5.subtitle: Form 18 Request & Technical Rebuttal
step5.description: Examination is initiated by filing Form 18 within 48 months. Patent examiners scrutinize statutory compliance and issue the First Examination Report (FER). The applicant must overcome all objections and cite rebuttals within 6 months.
step5.keyAction: File Form 18 & respond to First Examination Report

step6.title: Grant of Patent
step6.subtitle: Issuance of Certificate of Patent & 20-Year Term
step6.description: Upon overcoming all objections and pre-grant challenges, the patent is officially sealed under Section 43. Entered into the national Register of Patents, conferring 20 years of exclusive statutory protection and economic monopoly across India.
step6.keyAction: Official seal under Section 43 with 20-year exclusivity

items.question: What is AayuGranth?
items.answer: AayuGranth is a digital knowledge archive that brings together documented Indian traditional knowledge and intellectual property information. It helps users understand traditional knowledge, its documentation and its relationship with modern innovation and protection.

items.question: Why does traditional knowledge need protection?
items.answer: Traditional knowledge can be vulnerable to misuse, misappropriation and claims based on knowledge that has existed for generations. Proper documentation helps establish evidence of existing knowledge and supports defensive protection against inappropriate intellectual property claims.

items.question: How can AayuGranth help with patent research?
items.answer: AayuGranth helps users understand existing traditional knowledge and identify relevant prior art sources before pursuing an innovation. This can provide useful context for researchers, innovators and applicants conducting preliminary patent research.

items.question: What is the Indian patent process?
items.answer: The Indian patent process generally involves preparing and filing a patent application, examination by the Indian Patent Office, responding to examination requirements and proceeding toward grant when the legal requirements are satisfied. AayuGranth provides educational information to help users understand this process.

items.question: Can traditional Ayurvedic knowledge be patented?
items.answer: Traditional knowledge that is already publicly known generally cannot be claimed as a new invention simply by repackaging it. However, genuinely new and inventive developments involving traditional knowledge may raise separate intellectual property questions and should be evaluated under the applicable patent requirements.
